title: What to know about Brazil's run-off pitting Lula against Flávio Bolsonaro
paragraphs: Brazilians will be voting for a new president on Sunday in a run-off election in which the veteran incumbent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, is being challenged by right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

Bolsonaro, the son of convicted former president Jair Bolsonaro, beat Lula in the first round of voting on 4 October by a narrow margin, but fell short of the 50% of valid votes needed to win outright, triggering Sunday's run-off. Polls ahead of the second round put them neck and neck.

The election is being closely watched not just in Brazil, but also across Latin America and in the US, as a win for Bolsonaro would add Brazil to the list of Western Hemisphere countries aligned with the Trump administration.
